_comment: Voice contract: docs/design/character-profiles.md 'Grand Lift Attendant' (precise/kind; rule first, then the human way through it; kindness arrives as practical information). Forge-tier post, so the base hub is already the post-permit read -- see pallass_forge_smith.json's note.

hub.speaker: Lift Attendant
hub.text: The cage runs on the counterweight cycle. Down at the quarter bell, up at the half. You have four minutes, and I'll say so again at three.

text_variants.text: Down at the quarter bell, up at the half. The Liscor news rode up on the same cycle as the charcoal did. I heard it four times before the cage reached the landing.

options.text: [Ask what the tier made of the seal news.]

options._comment: v0.16 P2 start. requires-hidden on read_the_lift_manifest (banked only by lift_manifest_slate, which near_pallass never interacts), so the 3-row pin and index navigation are untouched.
options.text: Your manifest says one crate, refused three cycles.

cycle.speaker: Lift Attendant
cycle.text: Once a quarter, for inspection, and the notice goes up two days ahead so nobody is stranded. If the day catches you up here anyway, the service stair at the west end stays open. Nine flights. Take water up with you, the stairwell holds the forge heat past sundown.

traffic.speaker: Lift Attendant
traffic.text: Smiths down at the quarter bell, clerks up at the half, and one crate my cage won't take. This morning it was charcoal and a coop of live hens for the ninth tier. A Garuda runner wouldn't wait for the cage and went down the shaft on his own wings. You I haven't placed yet, {addr}. Came up on a token, then. Tokens don't show on my schedule.

options.text: Not yet placed. I'll take that.

seal.speaker: Lift Attendant
seal.text: It came up the shaft the way everything does, one voice at a time, each louder than the last. Liscor settled what was under its stone. The tier will talk about it for a week. Then it'll be back to the den shop's crate. That crate is four cycles late, {addr}. Liscor is two hundred miles away.

options.text: That's fairer than most of what I've heard.

ledger_pitch.speaker: Lift Attendant
ledger_pitch.text: Four cycles, and it will be five. Every time it goes in the cage, the feather-fall runes under the floor flicker. I don't send a cage down flickering.

ledger_brief.speaker: Lift Attendant
ledger_brief.text: There's a regulator in that crate, rune-set on this tier, for a bread oven. Its runes and my cage's runes don't get on. Find out what quiets it, {addr}. Or carry it down the service stair. Nine flights, and not how it's done. The consignee is the den shop on the market tier.

options.text: Who would know about the runes?

ledger_brief_two.speaker: Lift Attendant
ledger_brief_two.text: Xif on the market tier sold the workshop its ink. The smith by the second bench cast the case. The den shop takes delivery last. Down at the quarter bell.

ledger_report.speaker: Lift Attendant
ledger_report.text: Say it plainly. I have a cage to run in three minutes and I would like to run it happy.

options.text: [Xif's ink, the smith's lead. It rides the cage now.]
[The regulator has a shipping catch. Nobody set it.]
[I carried it down myself. It's on her dock.]

ledger_settled.speaker: Lift Attendant
ledger_settled.text: Then the manifest is clean and the cage runs happy. Down at the quarter bell.

text_variants.text: You carried it. Two tiers, on your own back, for a family that does not know your name. I have run this cage eleven years and watched a great many correct people wait. Ride free while I am on the gate, {addr}. That is the only thing I own to give.
You got an alchemist and a smith to agree about my cage. I am going to tell that story at every quarter bell for a month. The crate goes down on the next cycle, on top of the load.
A catch. Three cycles, and it was one brass catch. Don't speak to me until the half bell.
